institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I liked the profile of the university and that it mainly focies on organic agriculture and sustainability. I also have a good friend who stayed in Vienna for year and really liked it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. We were well welcomed and information was easy to get.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assigned a budy who contacted me before arrival and was happy to answar questions. We had multiple welcome days with lot of information and we could always contact a erasmus responsible via email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It seemed pretty difficult but i found a place through a friend who lived in Vienna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me it was great living with people outside campus and erasmus life. I lived in a very social flat where we did a lot of things together and it was great for feeling at home and getting to know the city .

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too difficult to find something outside campus if you dont have contacts.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult to find courses before arriving because the system, is confusing and you dont get acces to the course timetable before you arive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registering at campus is easy. You meet up on the office and get a card and so on. Registering for courses is a bit more difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write emails with questions and you got lot of information on the velcome days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I registered for more courses than I need and then went to the first lecture to see how it was before deciding. This was very commen and a great way to find the right courses. In general I was happy with the corses i ended up with. However, I found some of the small courses a bit superficial.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try the first lecture before you decide and dont get too stressed about the many courses and schedules. Some overlaps are okay. And do some excursions, they are great!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked that many of the courses were focused on sustainability and that it is easy to swap around and change courses. However the system is a bit confusing and stressfull. Also, many courses where more focused on social science than i was used to at a science university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My general experience was that the course level was lower than at KU but some courses did take more time for for example reeding and assignments than I was used to. For me reeeding up for exams also took more time than at KU because you have so many different courses and maybe shorter lectures meaning you had to read up on more yourself.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses were more divided into either lectures, seminars or excursions where it is more a mix at UCPH. You could therefore choose courses that was only excursions and field work or couses that was only lectures and not interactive at all. Therefore its a good idea to make sure you have a mix.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Soil fertility and soil ecology in organic agriculture
- Agroecology - A science, a practice and a movement
- Interdisciplinary excursion on organic agriculture
- Organic horticulture (vegetables and ornamentals)
- Stress physiology of plants
- Methods of measuring stress resistance in plants
- Agroforestry in mountain regions
- Case studies in organic grassland management
- European regulatory framework for organic production
- Intensive German Refresher Course - moderate advanced
- Multidisciplinary field trip in wildlife ecology
- Soil protection

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Soil fertility and soil ecology in organic agriculture had a good teacher and was interesting also with some field work and had an early exam. 

Agroecology - A science, a practice and a movement was a very different structured course with a lot of interesting reading material, discussions and group work. 

Interdisciplinary excursion on organic agriculture a 2 day excursion were we saw a lot of interesting organic farms. It was really well structures, inspiring and a lot of fun. 

Case studies in organic grassland management was also a really nice excursion to a great institute in the mountains, but a lot of group work online for the exam. 

Stress physiology of plants was a nice lecture class and i learned alot, but maybe some more workload than other 2 ECTS courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used the city a lot more than back home. Went to many cafees, bars and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many things are similar to Denmark.  Goung out for food and drinks/coffe is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There a really nice student bar driven by students that is open all day. The park and erea around campus is really nice and green.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was yoga, salsa and drumming lessons every week, either for free or very cheap. There was a really nice festival at campus arranged by TUWI the student bar organisation.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the TUWI festival and try out the salsa.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature around Vienna and go to the Heuriger (small wine cafees in the wine fields around the city). You can find cheap sport courses at the sport univerisity USI. Its nice to bike around in the city, but be carefull not to fall in the tram lanes. Go to donau insel in the summer and in winter try some of the small very cute cinemas all around the city. As a student you can see all the movies you like for 22€ a month in the small cinemas if you get the non-stop kino abo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy i would say

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do the excursions that are multible days and the seminars where there is group work-

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really? Just adjusting to being a new place and find new friends at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Theres a more layed back culture than in DK, and a big culture for going our for a drink in summer or a coffee in winter. And its really easy to find vegan and vegetarian and organic food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Campus and the people at campus arre really nice and layed back - theres a bit of a hippie vibe in the best way. 

Its nice with the many small courses eventhough it seems a bit confusing. 

Try and see if you can find housing outside campus,  it gives a lot to the exchange experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would reccoment getting a bike

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new friends and being more on your own in a new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first month as difficult because because i didnt know people very well and the winter is really cold and windy in Vienna, so it was a bit difficult exploring the city and finding things to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
